comments.content:
## FFe ##

[Description]

Merge Debian unstable 65.0-1 (upstream 65.0) as 65.0-1ubuntu1. stonking has 64.0-1ubuntu1 (FFe LP: #2165887).

Upstream v64.0..v65.0 (91 commits), highlights:
- mlx5: ConnectX-10 PCI IDs, clock and CQ cleanup fixes
- rdma_topo: ConnectX-9 ID, multi-NIC and NUMA topology support
- libibverbs: Completion Counters verbs, DMA-buf fd export for ibv_buf
- librdmacm: repoll_* API, epoll in librspreload, CM event fixes
- Provider updates: mana, efa, ionic, bnxt_re, erdma

ABI: no SONAME change, new symbols only. Private ABI bump (IBVERBS_PRIVATE_65) affects only libibverbs1 and ibverbs-providers from the same source, as in 64.0.

Ubuntu delta is unchanged: no pandoc and no man pages on i386.

[Rationale]

- NVIDIA GB300 Grace machines benefit from the mlx5 and rdma_topo updates.
- Intel IPU E2000 (irdma GEN3) systems can benefit from the libibverbs updates.
- Keeps 26.10 on the current upstream release, already in Debian, with no new delta.

[Regression potential]

- Consumers: ceph, dpdk, libfabric, openmpi, ucx, fio, libpcap, ...
- No ABI break. Main risk is in mlx5/mlx4/mthca CQ handling and librdmacm event dispatch.
- librspreload now also interposes epoll_*; this only affects apps run with LD_PRELOAD=librspreload.

[Testing]

- Builds: TODO (all arches; i386 exercises the man pages delta)
- Reverse-dependency autopkgtests: TODO (same 14 sources as for 64.0, see autopkgtest-rdeps.txt)
- Install and upgrade from 64.0-1ubuntu1 in stonking LXD: TODO (see install-upgrade.log)

comments.author: virtustom
comments.content:
The 65.0-1ubuntu1 test build FTBFS on armhf and i386:

  armhf: https://launchpad.net/~virtustom/+archive/ubuntu/rdma-core-65.0-stonking/+build/33608059
  i386:  https://launchpad.net/~virtustom/+archive/ubuntu/rdma-core-65.0-stonking/+build/33608060

Both fail while compiling the pyverbs comp_cntr module, which is new in 65.0:

  comp_cntr.c:5168:61: error: passing argument 2 of 'ibv_read_comp_cntr' from
    incompatible pointer type [-Wincompatible-pointer-types]
    expected 'uint64_t *' {aka 'long long unsigned int *'}
    but argument is of type 'long unsigned int *'

pyverbs declares the value as 'unsigned long' while verbs.h declares the
parameter as 'uint64_t *'. Those are the same type on 64-bit architectures
but not on 32-bit ones, so the mismatch only breaks armhf and i386.

This is not specific to the Ubuntu delta. Debian's own 65.0-1 fails the same
way on armhf and i386, while amd64, arm64 and ppc64el built fine:

  https://buildd.debian.org/status/package.php?p=rdma-core

It is tracked in Debian as #1148146 (severity: serious, tags: ftbfs patch)
and forwarded upstream as PR #1803, which is still open:

  https://bugs.debian.org/1148146
  https://github.com/linux-rdma/rdma-core/pull/1803

I am waiting for Debian to fix this and will merge the resulting upload
instead, so that the Ubuntu delta stays limited to the two remaining
changes listed in the description. I will update this bug with the build
and test results once that upload is available.
